reason: The order ended by its own terms on 1949-04-09, inclusive. Its last-running command is the standstill: from the date of the order, January 19, 1949, and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change except by agreement is to be made by Northwest Airlines, Inc., or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. The board's signed letter submitting its report to the President is dated 1949-03-10 according to the reviewed factual-event record recorded as a later event; I count the report as made on that date, so the thirty days after it end on April 9, 1949, and the order was spent from the end of that day. The exclusive reading, under which the standstill ends when April 9 begins, is the alternative. The held sources show the date of the letter and do not show when it reached the White House, so the date assumes the report was made when submitted. The report requirement (due within thirty days of the order, extended thirty days by an order of February 11, 1949 that the board's letter mentions but that is not held) was performed by that submission, and the creation of the board was carried out by its appointment on January 24, 1949. Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237), later revoked the order by number as one of the orders listed in its table, with no saving clause; that revocation came after the end recorded here and is a later event, not the first end, because the order had already run out under its own terms.
